Eight hooks, deliberately different, so the test has a range.

A test of three hooks that all say the same thing tells you nothing. The eight are written across kinds: a question, a confession, a comparison, a plain claim, a 'wait for it'. The shoot covers the ones you pick with us; the grid is built from them.

↳One axis per round

Round one tests hooks with the creator and format held steady. Round two holds the winning hook and tests creators. The brief says which axis is moving.

↳Written to be swapped

Each hook is written so it can sit on the same body of footage. A hook swap is the cheapest new ad an account can get.

↳Kept for the next round

Hooks that did not make the shoot stay in the brief for round two.

Two to five creators per brief, cast to differ on one thing.

Starter casts two creators per brief, growth four or five. They are cast to differ on the thing the round is testing: age, tone, setting, niche. You approve the shortlist, and each creator shoots the same hooks so the comparison is fair.

↳Cast on the axis

If the round tests tone, the creators differ in tone and match on everything else. If it tests setting, the kitchen and the car get the same script.

↳Same hooks, each creator

Every creator in the round shoots the same picked hooks, so a creator winning means the creator won, not the line.

↳Paid by us, once

Creators are paid out of your package fee on a set schedule. One contract, one invoice.

Formats cut per placement, so the account compares like with like.

A hook that wins on TikTok and loses on Reels may just have been cut wrong for Reels. Every variant is cut native for the placement it is testing in, captions burned in, so the format is a variable you control rather than noise.

↳Named variants

Each cut is named for its grid position: hook, creator, format, placement. The ad account's naming matches the brief, so the read is quick.

↳Native, not resized

9:16 for the placement, hook in the first frame, captions inside the safe area. Six placements, six cuts if the round needs them.

↳One revision round, included

Included on every package. Usually spent on captions, so that the caption is not the thing being tested by accident.

The grid is read with you, and the next brief is written from it.

On Growth and Scale, the month closes with a debrief: which hooks held attention, which creators carried the product, which formats the account should keep. It is not a deck for its own sake; it is the first page of the next brief.

↳Your numbers, our read

The performance data stays in your ad account. hypjam reads it with you and turns it into decisions: carry, retire, swap, scale.

↳Written into the brief

The next round's brief opens with the read: two more like hook 07, bring back the kitchen creator, drop the long format.

↳Honest about noise

Small tests are noisy. When a difference is not big enough to act on, the debrief says so rather than inventing a winner.

Built for the problems a testing budget actually has.

Not a pile of videos with a spreadsheet after. hypjam is built around the test that changed three things at once, the winner nobody can explain, and the debrief that never reached the next brief.

Three things changed at once

A new hook, a new creator and a new cut in the same ad means the winner cannot be explained. The brief moves one axis per round.

The winner nobody can explain

Named variants that match the ad account's naming make the read a five-minute job instead of an archaeology dig.

The debrief stayed in a deck

A read that does not change the next brief was a report, not a test. On Growth and Scale, it is the first page of round two.

Too small to call

Some rounds do not produce a clear winner. The debrief says so, and the next round is designed to find one.

Rights and safety

FAQ

Questions growth leads ask first.

↳How many variants does a round produce?

It depends on the package and the axis. A Growth brief with three picked hooks, four creators and two placements is twenty-four named variants from one shoot; the brief sets the number before anyone films.

↳Do you run the ads?

No. The spend and the account stay with your team. We deliver named variants cut per placement and read the results with you.

↳What if there is no clear winner?

Then the debrief says so. Small tests are noisy, and inventing a winner would make the next round worse. Round two is designed to separate the close ones.

↳Can we test with our own creators?

Yes. They shoot the same picked hooks as the roster creators in the round, on the same contract, so the comparison is fair.

↳How is a testing round priced?

By package: starter from £1,800 a month with six videos and two creators, growth from £3,600 with twelve videos and four or five creators. The final number is scoped once we know the grid.
